verses.1: A song of ascents. Out of the depths I call to you, LORD;
verses.2: Lord, hear my cry! May your ears be attentive to my cry for mercy.
verses.3: If you, LORD, mark our sins, Lord, who can stand?
verses.4: But with you is forgiveness and so you are revered.
verses.5: I wait with longing for the LORD, my soul waits for his word.
verses.6: My soul looks for the Lord more than sentinels for daybreak. More than sentinels for daybreak,
verses.7: let Israel look for the LORD, For with the LORD is kindness, with him is full redemption,
verses.8: And God will redeem Israel from all their sins.

notes.text: The depths: Sheol here is a metaphor of total misery. Deep anguish makes the psalmist feel "like those descending to the pit" (Psalm 143:7).
And so you are revered: the experience of God's mercy leads one to a greater sense of God.
